title: Mazatzal segment geometry
description: One segment's full-resolution line, at curation/geometry/<segment id>.json. Written by tools/build_geometry.py and regenerated wholesale on every run -- nothing here is authored. Valid GeoJSON: cum_m and derived are foreign members, which RFC 7946 permits, so any GeoJSON reader can draw the line while this project's own tools get the extras.

coordinates.description: Positions in GeoJSON order: longitude, latitude, elevation in metres. Elevation is resampled from the DEM (see docs/elevation.md), not the recorded value, and is null only where the DEM has no coverage. Longitude and latitude are rounded to 6 decimal places (~0.1 m) and every derived figure is computed from these rounded values, so the file reproduces its own numbers exactly.

cum_m.description: Cumulative distance in metres from the start of the line, one value per position, first always 0. This is what makes a segment addressable by fractional position, so a split at 0.62 is exact and needs no re-measuring (schema decision: partial legs). The last value times the metres-to-miles factor is the segment's miles in graph.json.

arc.description: Which stretch of which recorded track this line came from. Endpoint indices are into the immutable archive file, so the line can be rebuilt without re-guessing the arc -- a track can run between the same two junctions more than one way, and picking the right one was a human decision made in the curation tool.

track.description: Archive filename and track index within it, as '<file>#<n>'.

reversed.description: True when the segment's from -> to direction runs against the recorded direction of travel.

source.description: The recorded trip this leg was traced from. Mirrors segments[].sources[0] in graph.json.

elevation.description: Human-readable note on where the elevation channel came from.

gain_threshold_m.description: Threshold used for the gain_ft / loss_ft in graph.json. Recorded here because the figure is meaningless without it.

cleaning.description: The tools/clean.py settings that produced this line, so any output traces back to the parameters that made it.
